subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor RFC 0024 as its shared localization architecture, and which Gateway, recipient-locale, metadata, plugin, and release-gate contracts belong in the accepted v1 scope?
rationale: The design is technically coherent but commits multiple independently owned product surfaces, while prior localization direction was paused and repository policy requires explicit acceptance.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed foundation
options.body: Accept the locale registry, explicit locale context, structured message descriptor, English fallback, and coverage baseline first, while deferring owner-specific policies to follow-up decisions.

options.title: Sponsor the full program
options.body: Approve all five implementation stages and assign owners for Gateway, channels, metadata, plugin compatibility, translation review, and release gates.

options.title: Keep surfaces decentralized
options.body: Leave the RFC in draft or decline it and continue addressing localization through existing surface-specific pipelines and narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed foundation
recommendation.body: Accept the locale registry, explicit locale context, structured message descriptor, English fallback, and coverage baseline first, while deferring owner-specific policies to follow-up decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the strongest available prior product-direction signal on the canonical localization initiative.
